OECD faces $500 billion productivity loss due to ageism, report says

A report from the World Economic Forum (WEF) indicates that age-related discrimination within the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries could lead to a significant productivity loss. By 2040, this ageism is projected to cost the OECD approximately $500 billion. The issue stems from older workers being sidelined, preventing their full contribution to the economy.
